ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy SHA 75dc5aa9b428 introduced migration 0041_add_payment_retries_table.sql, which added a payment_retries table, and refactored retry.js and transaction.js to update both the payments and payment_retries tables within the same transaction. However, concurrent retry workers acquire row locks on these two tables in opposite order — retry worker A locks payments then payment_retries, while retry worker B (processing a related payment) locks payment_retries then payments — creating a classic AB-BA deadlock cycle. Under high retry concurrency (16 workers), deadlocks cascade: each rolled-back transaction is immediately re-queued and retried, causing the retry backlog to explode, connection pool to saturate at all 40 connections, and payment-service to return HTTP 503/500 at a 42% error rate.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately roll back deploy 75dc5aa9b428 to restore the previous retry logic (git revert or redeploy prior image tag). 2. As a short-term mitigation while investigating: reduce payment retry worker concurrency from 16 to 2 via environment variable PAYMENT_RETRY_CONCURRENCY=2 to reduce deadlock probability. 3. Add a consistent lock ordering fix to migration 0042: always acquire the payments row lock before the payment_retries row lock within the same transaction (enforce via advisory locks or explicit SELECT FOR UPDATE ordering). 4. Add a missing index on payment_retries(payment_id) if not present to reduce lock contention scan range. 5. Verify deadlock rate drops to 0 in postgres-exporter metrics before restoring full concurrency.
